scoring_justification: Full recompute (T1) is infeasible because the paper does not supply exact reference numerical values for average_z, sigma, or subband energies at the three specific densities; only qualitative trends and regime boundaries are described. The structural trends (decreasing average_z and sigma with increasing density, band energies positive and increasing) are verifiable and capture the paper's main physical claim about confinement regimes.

hidden_assets.purpose: Structural inequality thresholds for average_z, sigma, and layer_fractions[0] corresponding to low/mid/high density regimes.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from the paper's qualitative description of the confinement regimes. The paper states that in the low-density regime (<1e14 cm^-2) the 2DEG spreads over many layers, average_z > 20; in mid-range (1-5e14 cm^-2) confinement becomes pronounced, average_z < 15; in high-density regime (>5e14 cm^-2) more than 50% of the density is in the first layer and average_z < 5. These thresholds are extracted from Figures 4 and 8 and the text in Sections III-V.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Read from paper text and estimated from reported trends.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Thresholds correspond to the paper's own regime definitions and observed values; they are not arbitrary.

required.densities: array of objects each containing n_T, band_energies, layer_fractions, average_z, sigma

outputs.description: Confinement statistics: for each of the three densities, provides the six lowest 2D subband energies, per-layer fractional occupancy, average depth and spread. The checker will verify internal consistency and structural trends (e.g., average_z decreasing and sigma decreasing as density increases, high-density peak at layer 0) against expected confinement regimes.

output_contract.notes: The solver may exhibit run-to-run variations; the verifier uses relative trends and inequalities with moderate tolerances to accommodate legitimate implementation spread.
